howToCalculate.title: How to estimate CDB return
howToCalculate.p1: Enter the amount, calendar-day term, business days and CDB rate type. For CDI-linked CDBs, use the CDI percentage and an annual CDI expectation you enter yourself.
howToCalculate.p2: The calculator converts the annual rate to a 252-business-day daily rate, estimates gross value, then deducts IOF and IR according to calendar-day term.

preVsCdi.title: Fixed-rate CDB vs CDI-linked CDB
preVsCdi.p1: For fixed-rate CDBs, the simulation uses the annual fixed rate entered. For CDI-linked CDBs, the daily rate comes from your annual CDI expectation multiplied by the CDI percentage.
preVsCdi.p2: The tool does not fetch offers, rankings or current CDI; it only applies the assumptions you enter.

taxes.title: IR and IOF on CDB
taxes.p1: IOF may reduce returns on short redemptions up to 30 calendar days under the regressive table from Decree 6,306/2007.
taxes.p2: IR follows regressive rates of 22.5%, 20%, 17.5% or 15% by term and applies to positive yield after IOF.

oneHundredCdi.title: What 100% of CDI means
oneHundredCdi.text: A CDB at 100% of CDI follows the CDI rate used in the simulation. Since the rate is entered manually, the result depends directly on your annual CDI assumption.

fgc.title: FGC on CDB: what to watch
fgc.text: CDB/RDB appears among FGC-covered products, but the guarantee has limits, conditions and depends on the institution or conglomerate. Coverage does not change the return formula and does not remove every risk.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.p1: This tool estimates results from rates you enter. It does not fetch offers, recommend investments, or replace contract reading, income statements, or professional guidance.
disclaimer.p2: FGC has limits and conditions; check the official source before investing.

q1.question: How do I estimate a CDB at 100% of CDI?
q1.answer: Enter 100 in % of CDI and provide your annual CDI expectation. The calculator applies that rate over 252 business days, then estimates IR and IOF by calendar-day term.

q2.question: Does the calculator use the current CDI?
q2.answer: No. Annual CDI is a user-entered assumption; the tool does not fetch current rates or daily history.

q3.question: When does IOF stop being charged?
q3.answer: Under the table used in this version, the rate reaches zero on day 30. For terms above 30 days, estimated IOF is zero.

q4.question: Which IR rate applies to CDB?
q4.answer: The rate depends on calendar days: 22.5% up to 180 days, 20% from 181 to 360, 17.5% from 361 to 720 and 15% above 720 days.

q5.question: Does CDB have FGC guarantee?
q5.answer: CDB/RDB appears among covered products, but the guarantee has limits and conditions. It does not change return or make every investment risk-free.

q6.question: Do fixed-rate and CDI-linked CDBs use the same formula?
q6.answer: Both compound over business days, but the daily rate comes from different assumptions: annual fixed rate for fixed-rate CDBs and entered annual CDI times CDI percentage for CDI-linked CDBs.
